subject: MSA redlines: territorial scope & subcontractor insurance - clarifications
messages:
From: Michelle Sandoval <contracts@acme.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: territorial scope & subcontractor insurance

Hi David,

Thanks for sending the MSA — attached is our redline (redlined_MSA_Acme_v2.pdf). Two insurance items bubbled up from our procurement and risk teams that we need to confirm before moving to signature:

1) Territorial limitation: your MSA currently has a territory carve that reads "United States and Canada only." Our Ops team requires worldwide coverage for the services we intend to deploy in EMEA/APAC. Can Redwood confirm whether the insurer will agree to worldwide coverage? If not, what narrow language can we put in the order form to limit exposure while allowing rollout?

2) Subcontractors: we typically require that vendor insurance "names the customer as additional insured and extends coverage to subcontractors and agents performing services under the MSA." Your redline removes explicit subcontractor flow-through language. Please confirm whether Redwood can: (a) have the COI show Addl Insured status for Acme with the endorsement that extends to subcontractors; or (b) accept a clause that Redwood will require subcontractors to carry equal coverage and name Acme as addl insured. Which is operationally feasible given your Dedicated/Private offerings?

We also asked our broker to provide standard wording for the addl insured endorsement — attaching to the thread for your reference. If you can provide a sample COI and endorsement language that your broker would issue, that will speed review on our side.

Thanks — we have a narrow window this week to close the contract.

Best,
Michelle
Procurement Manager
Acme Logistics

Attachment: redlined_MSA_Acme_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 5 May 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines: territorial scope & subcontractor insurance

David —

Quick operational/insurance read from our side (copied Kimberly for legal language):

- Territory: Our standard broker position is to list the policy territory as "Worldwide (subject to sanctions/exclusions)." That is normally acceptable for customers deploying globally. If we needed a narrow order-form approach, Ops prefers a per-workload territory list (e.g., "Services in North America initially; EMEA to be added via written amendment"). The latter is workable but slows roll-out.

- Subcontractors / flow-through: Two practical options we can offer:
  * Option A — Broker endorsement (preferred): Redwood obtains an endorsement on the policy that extends Additional Insured status to customer and their affiliates and expressly extends to subcontractors engaged by Redwood for the covered operations. Many carriers will issue an "Additional Insured — Primary & Noncontributory — Endorsement" that references work performed by subs. We can ask broker to confirm the exact endorsement title; that is typically faster for the customer and centralized in our Risk team.
  * Option B — Contractual flow-down: Redwood contractually obligates its subcontractors to carry the same minimum limits and to name Acme as additional insured. This is operationally heavier (we must collect COIs from subs on a per-deployment basis) but avoids pushing the endorsement requirement into the primary policy where some carriers push back.

- Coverage minimums we recommend for this account (see COI-template-Redwood.pdf attached):
  * Commercial General Liability: $1,000,000 each occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate
  * Professional Liability / E&O: $1,000,000 each claim / $1,000,000 aggregate
  * Cyber / Privacy Liability: $2,000,000 aggregate (if handling customer data or hosting services)
  * Workers' Compensation: statutory

- Endorsement note: Some carriers will not write an endorsement that "expressly extends to subcontractors" without naming specific subs; in that case we can accept contractual flow-down + customer acceptance of a Redwood-subcontractor COI register.

Attachments: COI-template-Redwood.pdf, endorsement-sample.txt (attachment stubs).

Kimberly — suggested legal phrasing for the MSA or order form to present to Acme? If you can provide a short addendum clause we can send today, ideal.

—Marissa
Sr. Contracts & Risk Manager
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Sandoval <contracts@acme.com>, Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 May 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: territorial scope & subcontractor insurance

Michelle / Oliver —

Thanks for the redline and the quick turnaround. Appreciate the clarity — below are the practical options from our side so you can pick the path that works best for Acme:

1) Preferred (broker endorsement): Our broker can issue a policy endorsement naming Acme Logistics and its affiliates as Additional Insured and stating that the endorsement applies to liability arising out of work performed by Redwood and (where issued) Redwood's subcontractors. We'll ask the broker to provide the exact endorsement title and sample language; attached is our COI template and a sample endorsement excerpt (COI-template-Redwood.pdf, endorsement-sample.txt). If this satisfies your risk team, we can proceed to finalize.

2) Alternative (contractual flow-down): Redwood accepts a clause requiring Redwood to ensure that any subcontractor engaged to perform the Services shall carry insurance meeting the same limits and shall name Acme as an Additional Insured. In this case, we will provide a register of subcontractor COIs for review prior to go-live.

3) Territory: We can confirm that our policies are written on a worldwide territory basis in normal circumstances. If you prefer an order-form approach to limit initial deployments, we can insert a scope line in the Order Form such as: "Services initially limited to United States; additional territories to be added by written Amendment." Please note that option slows roll-out and may require an amendment later.

Next steps — tell us which option Acme prefers (Endorsement vs Flow-down + COI register) and whether you need the broker to produce a carrier-signed endorsement prior to countersignature. If you want the broker endorsement, I'll ask Risk to coordinate immediately and can share the draft endorsement this afternoon.

Thanks,
David
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: COI-template-Redwood.pdf (attachment stub), endorsement-sample.txt (attachment stub)
